```{webr}
#| context: setup

download.file(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasciencedojo/datasets/master/titanic.csv",
  "titanic.csv"
)

library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("titanic.csv")
```

# The Pipe
`%>%` is called the pipe: it just means "and then" -- like go home" %>% "watch anime" %>% "go to sleep", or in R, 
data %>% filter() %>% summarize() = take the data, and then filter it, and then summarize it.

Make sure you run every code block here to understand what each function is doing!

## Selecting a Column 
```{webr}
df %>% 
  select(Survived)
```

### Column to Vector 
Why would we want to select only a column? 
```{webr}
df %>% 
  pull(Survived)

survive_vector <- df %>% pull(Survived)
```

A vector is a different data type than a column. Now that we've put the `Survived` column into a vector, we can use our vector functions. 

```{webr}
mean(survive_vector)
```

## Selecting rows based on column value
```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(Sex == "female")
# Optionally turn this into its own dataframe: fem_df <- %>% filter(Sex == "female")
```

## Combining filter() and select()

```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(sex == "female") %>% 
  select(Age)
```

```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(sex == "male") %>% 
  select(Age)
```

```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(Pclass == 1) %>% 
  select(Sex)
```

## Selecting rows based on conditioning column value 
### Only show rows where the value in `Sex` is not `female` 
```{webr}
df %>% filter(sex != "female")
```

### Only show rows where the value in `Age` is greater than 10 
```{webr}
df %>% filter(age > 10)
```

### Only show rows where the value in `Age` is greater than 10 AND the value in `Sex` is `male` 
```{webr}
df %>% filter(age > 10 & sex == 'male')
```

# Full Examples 

Compare the outputs when you delete the row that says mean()
```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(sex == "female") %>% 
  select(Survived) %>% 
  mean()
```

```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(sex == "female") %>% 
  select(Survived) %>% 
  summary()
```

```{webr}
df %>% 
  filter(sex == "male") %>% 
  select(Survived) %>% 
  summary()
```
